metadata.title: Effectiveness of integrated STEM and problem-based learning in improving students’ conceptual understanding in science

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study used a quasi-experimental one-group pretest–posttest design with a total-enumeration sample from a single intact Grade 11 STEM class in a public SHS in the Philippines (n = 38). The manuscript does not report the use of any complex survey design weights (e.g., student sampling weights) or replicate weights, and the analysis is conducted at the classroom level rather than using an international large-scale assessment sampling frame. Because the dependent variable is a researcher-developed two-tier Meaningful Conceptual Understanding (MCU) test score (0–20) administered to the same students at two time points, standard ILSA-style weighting for population representativeness is not applicable. The only explicit preprocessing described is assumption checking for the paired-samples t-test (outlier screening via boxplot and normality checks), with no missing-data imputation strategy reported.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values are not applicable because the study does not use ILSA/PISA/TIMSS achievement scales with PV-based scoring; instead, it uses a classroom-administered, two-tier MCU test (0–20) developed for Grade 11 General Biology 1 biomolecules. The paper also does not describe any missing-data handling procedure for the MCU scores, likely because the analysis is based on the intact class with pretest and posttest administered to the same students. This omission is a reporting gap for missingness transparency, but it does not affect the PV applicability decision.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Participants were selected using total-enumeration sampling from one intact Grade 11 STEM class enrolled in General Biology 1 during the study term. The class was purposively selected because (1) General Biology 1 was offered that term, (2) the school approved a six-week in-class implementation, and (3) the intact Grade 11 STEM composition aligned with the module’s scope, schedule, and target competencies. The instructional focus was biomolecules using a contextualized Pili (Canarium ovatum) problem, and the MCU test was administered as both pretest and posttest to the same students. The manuscript does not report additional exclusions (e.g., incomplete test forms) or any missing-data rules.

main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Primary study outcome (heuristic migration), finding that This quasi-experimental one-group pretest–posttest study evaluated a six-week integrated STEM delivered through problem-based learning (I-STEM-PBL) for Grade 11 General Biology 1 (biomolecules) in a single public SHS classroom in the Philippines (n = 38). The outcome was a researcher-developed 20-item two-tier Meaningful Conceptual Understanding (MCU) test scored 0–20, with conceptual understanding operationalized across concept connections, explanation/justification, application/transfer, and misconception diagnosis. Students’ total MCU scores increased from M = 4.81 (SD = 2.00) to M = 6.14 (SD = 2.43), t(37) = 2.89, p = .007, Cohen’s d = 0.48, with a normalized gain g = 0.08; the Proteins & Enzymes facet improved significantly (t(37) = 2.65, p = .012) while Carbohydrates & Lipids did not (t(37) = 1.37, p = .180). The study reports no machine-learning models, no survey weights, and no missing-data handling procedure, so results are context-bound and causal claims are limited by the lack of random assignment. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: The extraction is sparse for ML-specific fields because the manuscript is not an empirical machine-learning/predictive modeling study on ILSA microdata. It uses a classroom intervention with paired-samples t-tests and descriptive/qualitative analyses of MCU scores and reviewer evaluations, so there are no ML algorithms, PV handling, or survey-weighting components to extract. Consequently, main_findings and confounders_identified are left empty rather than fabricated.
